reviewTraps: Animal models are shared2027 content, unlike the legacy HL extension.
All four contexts apply to both levels; context subheadings are organizational, not exact official exam-question labels.
A chosen disorder/process/theory is an example selection; do not require every possible example as compulsory recall. Supply unfamiliar model details when needed.
P1A has no specified context; P1B is applied to a supplied scenario; P1C does not reward study-detail memorization.
P2A is about the student’s own class practical. A bank item using a supplied practical record is an explicit practice adaptation, not an exact reproduction of this exam demand.
P2B must name at least four concepts and allow discussion of at least two.
Direct graph/statistical/thematic analysis is HL-assessed, not a sharedSL exam skill.
P3 needs quantitative AND qualitative sources, a named extension/context, and at least three sources for synthesis.
Do not imply correlation establishes causation, random sampling equals random allocation, or group culture averages determine individual traits.
Keep raw data, plot labels, uncertainty/error-bar meaning, sample sizes, statistic values, direction and measurement scales consistent.
Synthetic datasets and interview extracts must be explicitly labelled; do not attach invented data to a named real study.
Avoid clinical overclaims such as a simple universal chemical-imbalance cause; represent evidence, alternative explanations and limits.
Historical animal evidence can be discussed, but students must not conduct/propose animal IA research. Class practicals and the hypothetical IA have different ethical boundaries.
Research proposal tasks need methodological justification, not fabricated completed results.

Two separate review roles must verify every complete question, exemplar answer, indicative content, rubric and figure. Uncalibrated medium/hard labels are editorial, not official IB difficulty or grade boundaries.
